statement: Al-Isra' is the night journey to Jerusalem; al-Mi'raj is the ascent through the heavens.
The date is disputed; it occurred in Makkah before the Hijrah.
alternatives: Dates given range from the year revelation began to a year or sixteen months before the Hijrah; 27 Rajab is popular but not established. Al-Mubarakpuri lists six opinions.

statement: Anas's narration: al-Buraq described; he rode to Jerusalem, tethered it to the ring used by the prophets, prayed two rak'ahs in the mosque; Jibril brought wine and milk, he chose milk, 'you have chosen the fitrah'.
notes: Direct speech. Content machine-checked in the Muslim dataset (dataset no. 411). Abd al-Baqi number from memory. Al-Buraq is described in his words but is never depicted (SPEC 36.2).

statement: At each heaven Jibril was asked who he was and who was with him; the welcome; he met Adam, Yahya and Isa, Yusuf, Idris, Harun, Musa, Ibrahim in the first to seventh heavens; then was raised to Sidrat al-Muntaha.
notes: Machine-checked for the opening and the first heaven; the order of the prophets follows Bukhari 3887 from memory (349 differs slightly in which heaven Ibrahim and Musa are placed). Reviewer to confirm.

statement: Fifty prayers were enjoined; Musa advised him to ask for reduction; after repeated returns they became five; he said he had asked until ashamed, and was content and submitted.
notes: Direct speech of Musa and of the Prophet from memory of Bukhari 3887; the dataset text was truncated at lookup. Reviewer to check wording.

statement: Quraysh disbelieved; the caravan journey to Jerusalem took about a month each way.
notes: Their disbelief is in Bukhari 3886; the month's journey is from the Seerah reports.

statement: He said: when Quraysh disbelieved me I stood in al-Hijr and Allah displayed Jerusalem to me and I described it while looking at it.
People went to Abu Bakr; he said if he said it, it is true, and that he believed him about news from heaven; he was called as-Siddiq from then.
notes: Recorded by al-Hakim from Aishah; grading disputed. Narrated with attribution.
